analysis:
Changes: docs/developer/test.md (date bump; new documentation at lines 542-566 for ModelCheckpointConversationLiveTests) and a new opt-in live test, ModelCheckpointConversationLiveTests.swift. I examined the docs text at head lines 489-566 and the patch for the new test file. Only a bounded patch excerpt of the Swift file was visible, and no head_text unit was supplied for it, so I could not inspect its full body.

Security-relevant behavior: the documented command uses `env -i` with a minimal environment. It requires an isolated ephemeral cache and public synthetic prompts. It is gated by DARKBLOOM_CHECKPOINT_CONVERSATION_BENCHMARK=1 and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_EXCLUSIVE_GPU=1, and the report contains timings, token counts, file counts and byte counts, not content or keys. The test sets DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_MAX_STAGE_MB for the run only. It is test-only code in the Tests target and changes no production source, so it does not alter the T-041 SSD cache gate, TTL, disk budget, name derivation or AAD. The patch comment and docs say the test requires an ephemeral cache. The docs do not explicitly say never to use production cache roots or keys, although the neighboring text at line 486 does. This is a minor documentation gap, not a finding.

Residual questions: the full Swift file could not be seen. The next pass should confirm that it uses an isolated ephemeral cache root and key, never the production darkbloom/kv3 root or the persistent KEK. It should also confirm that the report does not record prompt text and that the output path is written safely. The patch excerpt shows only synthetic public records and a Codable report with no content fields. No threat-model regression was identified from the visible evidence.
